observed: The Homebrew Cask/Formula generator and validator are implemented and deterministically tested end to end, without ever running brew, a signing tool, or a cargo/pnpm/Tauri build. scripts/release/homebrew/generate.mjs derives every field from two real RightKit inputs only: a read-only dynamic import of apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs (app, version, installer artifact -> R2 key map), and a real RightKit sealed release manifest for one explicit --commit, whose recorded per-file SHA-256/size are independently re-verified against the artifact bytes on disk before being trusted. The public download URL is derived by joining the sealed manifest's R2 key with the same RIGHTAPPS_PUBLIC_DOWNLOAD_BASE constant/env-var @rightkit/release/upload-release.mjs itself uses -- never invented. renderCask()/renderFormula() only produce real Homebrew Ruby DSL (on_arm/on_intel blocks for the Cask; on_macos + Hardware::CPU.arm? branching plus a `service do` block for the Formula's crypt-service daemon) when BOTH mac-arm64 and mac-x64 resolve to real, validated (https URL + lowercase sha256 + semver) data; otherwise both fall back to the exact already-committed 'intentionally unavailable' placeholder text (packaging/homebrew/Casks/membrane.rb and Formula/membrane.rb, unchanged by this task, asserted byte-identical by test). validateCaskSource/validateFormulaSource structurally reject an embedded url/sha256/real version while not ready, :no_check, :latest, and -- once ready -- require an exact match against the resolved per-architecture URL/SHA-256 for both architectures, never just one. All 15 tests in tests/platform/macos/homebrew-generate.test.mjs pass, covering: the real (not fixture) apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs proving today's declared arm64-only/no-headless-target gap; a single-arch sealed-manifest fixture proving mac-x64 stays explicitly blocked (never silently assumed) even when mac-arm64 resolves for real; a tamper/hash-mismatch fixture proving a sealed file that doesn't match its manifest-recorded SHA-256 fails closed before any Cask is generated; an unsealed/malformed-manifest fixture failing closed; a dual-arch fixture (synthetic, clearly labeled, never presented as real) proving the ready/real-render code path handles both architectures explicitly end to end; malformed-data rejection even when ready is force-set true; and CLI-level tests for `plan`, `render`, and `validate` covering argument validation, fail-closed behavior on a missing sealed manifest, and no-file-written-without-an-explicit---out. As a read-only, non-automated sanity check (recorded in commands.log, not part of the hermetic test suite), `plan` was additionally run against a genuine local .right-release/sealed/membrane-hub-0.1.5-0d5e7077/mac/ output from an earlier real `right-release build --platform mac` run, and correctly resolved the real arm64 DMG's real SHA-256 and derived URL while correctly reporting mac-x64 and both Formula architectures as blocked with the stated reasons. Real acceptance -- brew install/upgrade/uninstall/doctor actually passing on a clean Intel machine and a clean Apple Silicon machine -- requires a real signed x86_64/Intel mac build target (does not exist in apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs today), a real headless CLI/daemon release target for the Formula (also does not exist), uploading the sealed installer(s) to the public R2 bucket, and Adrian's explicit decision to publish the Cask/Formula and open a tap PR -- none of which this task performed, ran, or was permitted to perform. Status is recorded as pending_book_gate, not pass, per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md: this task does not execute the manifest command and does not claim acceptance pass.
